The nucleus

Series I: the deuteron bound at one Link and free at three, the alpha square sheared apart; the strong rows' escape clicks at the lifetime.

A registered world, examples/events/nucleus/deuteron_1.json, run as it is declared; its register entry is I, the nucleus (2026-09-20). Nothing was changed in the world and nothing is pinned by this page.

Also registered here: examples/events/nucleus/deuteron_3.json and examples/events/nucleus/alpha_square.json, the same series, run as declared. He-5 (the register's I9, the core family) was cut from series I for the budget and never run; it is not drawn.

The GameBoard

An open cube of 21 x 21 x 21 Nodes, K = 1 048 576, N = 64, the width of the push 2^28, the contact through the table. Three free families without a phase circle: p (charge 4), n, and nuclear with the column strong of value G = 10 000 and the sign minus and the lifetime 3. A proton is a free body of 1836 units of p holding one unit of nuclear (M 1837, Q 7344, G 10 000); a neutron 1839 of n holding one (1840, 0, 10 000); every body releases one row of its held content per direction of the 290 primitive directions with |a| + |b| + |c| at most 6 per interval. No detector is declared: the bodies are the external things whose read and contact records are the readings, the six faces and the border lifetime the detectors of what leaves. In deuteron_1 p is at (10, 10, 10) and n at (11, 10, 10); in deuteron_3 at (9, 10, 10) and (12, 10, 10), each kicked outward by 10^12; in alpha_square p1 (10, 10, 10), n2 (11, 10, 10), n3 (10, 11, 10), p4 (11, 11, 10).

the p rowsthe n rowsthe nuclear rows (the strong column, lifetime 3)a proton (a body of p)a neutron (a body of n)

Why this page

The owner asked to see the nucleons: bound, and coming apart. In this law a nucleus is bodies at adjacent Nodes reading each other's rows through the one coupling, a signed inner product over the columns the families declare (gravity, the charge, the strong column), and the strong column has a range that is a lifetime: a nuclear row clicks on the border at the age 3, so a body three Links away reads no strong row at all. A body that would step onto the other's Node is refused and hands its momentum component over through the occupant's table (the contact): the bound pair's labels are handed back and forth and return to 0, and nothing steps.

Bound: the deuteron at one Link

What to see: from the second interval each body reads the other's rows and is pushed toward it by 310 967 280 640 label units per interval (the register's designed integer, the n rows 10 161 754 944 and the nuclear rows 300 805 525 696); the gold halo is the strong rows within three Links, clicking on the border lifetime at 580 per interval from the fourth interval (1 738 260 over the run's 3000: run.json, the border's clicks); the pair never steps in 3000 intervals; its hand-overs: 327 (contact lines), the label 0 after each. The escape click at the lifetime is the strong force's range, seen at the border.

Free: the deuteron at three Links, kicked

What to see: no strong row reaches three Links (the reads of nuclear: 0), gravity alone pulls by 1 067 524 788 per interval on p (the register), far below the kick of 10^12; the first steps are at the intervals body 1 at the interval 33 from (9, 10, 10) to (8, 10, 10); body 2 at the interval 34 from (12, 10, 10) to (13, 10, 10); the bodies leave: body 2 through face:+x at 311; body 1 through face:-x at 346.

Coming apart: the square p n / n p

What to see: the square's bonds are central pushes and the contacts frictionless, and the p-p diagonal bond is weaker than the n-n one by exactly Q^2 x U_d, so the rows are sheared apart (the register: 49 090 283 970 per row per interval); the first steps: body 1 at the interval 95 from (10, 10, 10) to (10, 9, 10); body 2 at the interval 89 from (11, 10, 10) to (11, 11, 10); body 3 at the interval 110 from (10, 11, 10) to (10, 10, 10); body 4 at the interval 81 from (11, 11, 10) to (11, 12, 10); the bodies leave: body 2 through face:+x at 275; body 4 through face:-x at 285; body 1 through face:+x at 336; body 3 through face:-y at 339. The register's alpha is the line p n n p (alpha_line), which holds for 3000 intervals; the square does not.
